messages:
riya.s: alert: users reported unexplained queries against prod_metrics db from an ephemeral CI role. detected ~12:02 UTC. suspicious token reuse :rotating_light:
leeops: copying logs now, grabbing session id and pod names. tagging @sec-oncall
mike_p: any immediate customer impact?
riya.s: metrics look read-only but volume is high -> possible credential leak from CI job artifact. no writes observed.
devops-bot: automated alert: [AUTH] ephemeral-token used by service-account:ci-runner-prod to access metrics-db.read at 12:01:58 UTC (src: 34.72.11.9). request-id: req-9f4c.
sec-oncall: ack. recommended immediate steps: 1) revoke ephemeral role bindings 2) rotate vault role/issuer 3) add denylist for the token's jti 4) block source ip at firewall if persistent.
leeops: running quick revoke: 
```
# revoke ephemeral role for CI runner
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/ci-runner-prod revoke=true
kubectl -n ci delete rolebinding ci-runner-prod-binding
```
leeops: done. vault responded 204. rolebinding deleted.
mike_p: rotated OIDC trust? the CI issues tokens from our OIDC provider, might need to rotate client secret or disable provider temporarily.
riya.s: audit shows the token's jti used across 5 distinct pods over ~4m window. looks like it was embedded into a cached pipeline image.
auditsvc: audit-log: "principal=service-account:ci-runner-prod action=metrics-db.read resource=prod_metrics rowcount=1473 jti=8a7f... src=34.72.11.9 session=req-9f4c"
sec-oncall: I'll spin up a short-lived deny rule on infra firewall for 34.72.11.9 and add a cluster network policy to block egress from the implicated build pods.
leeops: firewall rule in place. cluster networkpolicy added (deny egress to metrics-hosts for pods with label pipeline_cache=true).
mike_p: we should blacklist the specific jti at the auth layer. how do we add jti deny in vault?
leeops: current workaround: add jti to our token-denylist table in redis and update auth middleware. I'll open a patch shortly.
riya.s: forensics: saving full pipeline image and build logs, creating an isolated copy of the image for analysis. suspicious file: /ci/cache/creds.json found in image layer.
sec-oncall: file noted. treat this as P1. notify legal and CISO. prepare disclosure timeline.
mike_p: short-term remediation checklist: 
- rotate any long-lived service keys referenced by CI jobs
- purge stale images from registry and re-run pipelines with fresh images
- add scan rule to CI lint that prevents plain creds in images
- add ephemeral token TTL enforcement on issuer side (<=5m)
leeops: patch deployed to auth service to reject jti values from redis denylist. patch id: PR#4231. rolling restart auth pods.
devops-bot: deploy status: auth v2.11 -> success. 3/3 pods ready.
riya.s: can we confirm no other tokens with same jti used elsewhere? auditsvc: running wide scan across last 48h.
auditsvc: scan result: only one jti match. additional related tokens issued for ci-runner-prod show normal patterns but different jti.
sec-oncall: next steps: 1) notify infra and product owners 2) rotate vault roles used by CI, rotate any referenced KMS access keys 3) add SCIM/CI policy to prevent credentials in image layers 4) longer term: require image provenance attestation + SBOMs
mike_p: I'm drafting the incident summary. will include timeline and list of mitigations. tagging @legal and @privacy for advice.
riya.s: thanks all. will keep thread updated after forensic analysis. if anything else odd appears, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
